🚨🇲🇽 <u>TWO PRIORITY TARGETS DOWN: ARELLANO FÉLIX AND CJNG LEADERS CAPTURED</u>

Federal forces captured two priority targets in coordinated operations: "El Kado," regional leader of the Arellano Félix cartel, in Valladolid, Yucatán, and "El Payaso," a CJNG operator tied to drug distribution, arms trafficking and money laundering, in Bahía de Banderas, Nayarit.

Navy, Army, SSPC and FGR working together. No foreign boots needed — Mexican institutions doing the job.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>PLAN B IS ALREADY MOVING: MEXICO'S EU DEAL AS SHIELD AGAINST USMCA UNCERTAINTY</u>

Trump wants the USMCA on annual review until 2036 — permanent uncertainty as leverage. Mexico's answer is diversification: the modernized agreement with the European Union, a bloc that bought $23.8 billion in Mexican exports and invested $9.9 billion in the country in 2025. Bilateral trade with Europe already totals $88.3 billion.

Martín Esparza in Contralínea: "Plan B cannot wait."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>VERACRUZ BACKS CANE GROWERS AS SUGAR EXPORTS TO THE US JUMP OVER 500%</u>

Mexico's sugar deal with the United States keeps bearing fruit. Veracruz — source of 40% of national production — will give political, economic and social backing to its cane growers as exports climb to 1.1 million tons in 2026-2027, a surge of more than 500%, Governor Rocío Nahle announced.

The state is even studying the reactivation of three shuttered sugar mills out of its 22.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>"WE ARE ADVANCING IN THE USMCA REVIEW": SHEINBAUM AFTER 90-MINUTE MEETING WITH GREER</u>

President Sheinbaum received US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer at the National Palace as the third round of talks closed. Her message after 90 minutes: "We are advancing in the review of the USMCA and in bilateral agreements."

Washington wants the treaty under annual review until 2036. Mexico arrived having done "everything humanly possible" to negotiate from strength.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>US KEEPS TARIFFS ON MEXICO UNCHANGED AFTER THIRD T-MEC ROUND: EBRARD</u>

While Trump hit Canada with 50% tariffs on autos, alcohol and dairy this week, Mexico closed the third round of USMCA talks with its tariffs untouched. Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard confirmed it: 85% of Mexican exports will keep entering the US market at zero tariff.

Negotiation, not submission — and it keeps working.

🇲🇽🎨 16,289 young people — 5,761 from the US — entered Mexico's binational music contest for peace "Through this binational contest between Mexico and the United States for young people aged 18 to 29, we have brought together and united young people from Mexico and the United States, and strengthened bonds that clearly exist on both sides of the border. Music has no borders. More than 16,289 young people participated: 10,528 from Mexico, 5,761 from the United States." — Culture Secretary Claudia Curiel, morning press conference The Culture Ministry announced results of the second edition of "México Canta," a contest for original music without violent lyrics. The seven US semifinalists perform August 23 at Los Angeles' Million Dollar Theater; the final is September 13 at the Auditorio Nacional.

🇲🇽✊ El Bogueto at the National Palace: "You can achieve great things coming from the barrio" ""I want the message for those from the barrio, for people everywhere, to get motivated, to take the initiative to fulfill their dreams. It doesn't matter where you're from, it doesn't matter what people say or where you come from. If you don't have opportunities, here is clear proof that you can achieve great things coming from the barrio."" — El Bogueto, at the morning press conference Armando Toledo Rosas, "El Bogueto," an independent artist from Ciudad Nezahualcóyotl with over 24 million streams who never went through the music industry's circuits, joined the government's "México Canta" contest voluntarily as an ambassador. He performed his song "Mi Barrio" at the July 23, 2026 press conference alongside the seven Mexican-American semifinalists.

🇲🇽🎨 Sheinbaum on bans of narco-glorifying music: education, not prohibition — "if you prohibit it, people will keep listening anyway" ""On this we believe it is better to promote and raise awareness, not to prohibit. Because if you prohibit it, people will keep listening to it anyway. So it is really about education."" — President Sheinbaum, morning press conference Several Mexican states and municipalities have banned public performances of music that glorifies crime. Asked whether those bans fit her government's message, Sheinbaum said the federal approach is promotion and awareness rather than prohibition, while recognizing each state's right to legislate. She contrasted it with the junk food ban in schools, where the government did set limits to protect children's health.
